system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:48:44 UTC, the domain controller recorded a service-ticket request for FILE-HD-01$ using svc-bkp, originating from public IP 45.79.19.196.

The external-origin svc-bkp authentication is inconsistent with the stated environment: there is no VPN, remote administration is limited to WS-OHADDAD-01, and svc-bkp is identified as a backup agent account on FILE-HD-01. This supports treating the activity as malicious unless an authorized explanation is verified.

At 13:46:06 UTC, FILE-HD-01 made an SMB connection to DC-HD-01; the domain controller recorded an anonymous NTLM network logon associated with that connection. The Zeek record reports only 5,155 origin bytes and 3,124 response bytes.

known_telemetry_limitations: FILE-HD-01 winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, including the alert time; process attribution and host-side activity during that period are therefore missing.
PROXY-HD-01 proxy collection was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, limiting visibility into proxied outbound destinations and transfer details.
The available records do not identify the process responsible for the flagged large transfer or document its destination, contents, or exact volume.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish that the svc-bkp ticket request caused, or was directly related to, the flagged transfer.
The evidence does not establish that the flagged transfer was an authorized CobaltVault backup upload or that it was data exfiltration.
The evidence does not establish whether 45.79.19.196 belongs to an authorized service provider or whether the ticket was subsequently used to access FILE-HD-01.
additional_evidence_needed: Identify the owner and purpose of 45.79.19.196; verify whether this source is authorized to authenticate as svc-bkp.
Review domain-controller authentication and service-access records, plus FILE-HD-01 and firewall/network logs, to determine whether the ticket was used and what connections followed.
Recover FILE-HD-01 process, service, task, and file-access telemetry for 13:30–14:10 UTC, especially around 13:46–13:49.
Obtain network-flow or packet evidence and proxy records for the flagged transfer, including destination, byte counts, and timing.
Verify CobaltVault agent execution and upload/job logs for the alert interval, and compare the recorded transfer with the approved backup behavior.
